transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Stop the wash only if you can do so without going near the wet plug or socket; otherwise isolate the washing-machine circuit at the consumer unit/fuse box. Do not touch or unplug it while water is near the socket, and keep people and pets away from the area. Mop up only once the electricity is safely isolated, using towels and keeping clear of the socket area. Do not use the machine again: it needs a qualified appliance engineer to inspect it after a leak has reached the electrical area. The leak may be from a loose/split inlet or drain hose, the pump/filter area, door seal, detergent drawer overflow from excess foam, or an internal hose/pump leak. After isolation, the useful clue is where the water first appears: drawer/front, door, rear hoses, or directly from underneath.

ok the consumer unit is in the hall and the floor there is dry so I can get to it. I'm standing in socks on the wet floor right now though, should I just go and switch it off? the water has definitely run back towards the socket

Do not walk across the wet floor in socks or touch the machine, plug or socket. Only go to the consumer unit if you can step directly onto a completely dry route/floor without crossing the water; then switch off the washing-machine circuit (or the main switch if you cannot identify its circuit). If there is no dry route, do not attempt it—move away from the water if you can do so safely and arrange urgent help from an electrician/emergency electrical service. Once isolated, leave the machine off and do not use it again until a qualified appliance engineer has inspected it, because water has reached the socket area. The leak could be a rear hose, pump/filter area, door seal, detergent-drawer overflow or an internal hose; it is not safe to investigate until the electrical risk is dealt with.

I'm already standing in the wet bit in my socks, so I don't think there's a completely dry way out without stepping through it. Should I just step out of the water as quick as I can and then go to the hall? I'm panicking a bit, the machine's still running

Do not take normal steps or run through it. Keeping your feet close together, shuffle/slide carefully to the nearest dry floor without touching the machine, any metalwork, the plug or socket; once dry, go straight to the consumer unit and switch off the washing-machine circuit, or the main switch if you are unsure which circuit it is. If you feel any tingling/shock, see sparks or smoke, cannot reach dry ground safely, or are injured, stop trying to deal with it and call 999; for an electrical network emergency in the UK, call 105. Once power is isolated, likely causes include a hose, pump/filter-area leak, door seal, detergent-drawer overflow or an internal hose leak, but do not investigate near the plug/socket.
ok I'll shuffle out to the dry bit then go to the hall and switch it off. no sparks or tingling or anything, no burning smell either. what do I do after that?

Once you are on dry flooring, switch off the washing-machine circuit at the consumer unit; use the main switch if you cannot identify it. Do not return to the wet area or touch the plug/socket, machine or any pooled water until the power is isolated. After that, keep the machine off and arrange a qualified appliance engineer to inspect it before it is used again, as water has reached the electrical area. The common causes are a split or loose inlet/drain hose at the rear, a leak around the pump/filter or an internal hose underneath, and less often a door-seal or detergent-drawer overflow. From a dry position only, the useful observation is where the water seems to have begun: rear connections, front/drawer area, or straight from underneath.
ok I've shuffled out and switched it off at the fuse box, so it's stopped. From what I can see the water is mostly coming from the front, under the door. Is that any help?

Yes, that is helpful: water appearing at the front makes the door seal, detergent-drawer overflow and the pump/filter area more likely than a rear hose. Once it is safe to approach and dry, an engineer can trace the actual source; water at the front does not prove it is the door seal. A useful prevention tip afterwards is to avoid overfilling the detergent drawer and use the stated detergent dose, as excess foam can force water out of the drawer/front. Is there anything else you need help with?

candidates: External water leak, commonly from a hose, pump/filter area, door seal or detergent drawer/oversudsing (high)
Internal hose, pump or tub leak (medium)
